How this works and what the terms mean

Ready result = finished work that met the same stated quality rule on both routes.

Full recurring cost = provider spend + shared infrastructure included in the review + human review and correction.

Cost per ready result = full recurring cost ÷ results that met the quality bar.

Evidence check = the required cost, quality, policy, and coverage checks that must agree before a difference can be called savings.

Finance recommendation = fund the change, fix the evidence, stop the change, or report insufficient evidence. It is bounded to this review.

Observed logs, samples, estimates, and missing evidence remain visibly different. A sampled or user-estimated result cannot become proven savings.

      Start with one bill

      For a simple subscription or invoice, enter the bill below. No CSV is required.

      Purchased usage credits? Check how to treat a prepayment

      A credit purchase receipt records cash paid in advance, not the cost of work completed on the invoice date. Do not enter the purchase as provider cost for that work. Review the purchase and remaining balance separately; attributing consumed credits to a period or workload needs usage records.

      Have a previous bill? Compare two periods locally

      Enter a previous amount for the same provider, account, workload, currency, and gross or net basis. Invoice dates alone do not establish comparable service periods.

      Both service periods must be supplied, complete, and non-overlapping. Equal lengths allow a raw bill change; different lengths show calendar-day amounts as a reference only. Fixed monthly plans can differ per day because of month length. Neither comparison proves a cause or savings.

      Have a budget for this bill? Check it against the same period

      Use a budget for this bill's provider, account, workload, currency, and declared service period. A monthly budget cannot be compared with an annual invoice or an unknown service period.

      This is a one-time check of entered amounts. AI Cost Lens does not monitor spend or send budget alerts.

      An invoice proves cost, not usage or outcomes. Missing requests, tokens, retries, and human effort stay unavailable. One bill cannot establish savings. Add detailed usage later only when it is useful.

      OpenAI API

      Claude API

      Use the Anthropic Messages Usage Report for tokens and the Cost Report for provider cost. Anthropic’s report does not include a request count, so get that from your application or gateway logs.

      Amazon Bedrock

      Use Cost Explorer or CUR for billed cost and Bedrock invocation logs for requests and tokens. Match them by model and reporting period.

      Gemini or Vertex AI

      Use Cloud Billing reports or a billing export for cost, plus Vertex AI or application logs for requests and tokens. Keep the project and date range aligned.

      Gateway or another tool

      Use its cost and usage export. If cost comes from one system and usage from another, group both to the same route and reporting period before copying the totals.

      Show me exactly what to put in each column
      periodbaseline or proposed.
      dateThe date of that report bucket in YYYY-MM-DD format. Keep provider cost and usage grouped the same way.
      workloadYour plain language name for the work. Use the exact same name on both routes.
      providerThe company or platform that served the model, such as Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, Google Cloud, OpenAI, or your gateway.
      modelThe reported model name. Use “Mixed models” only when the source report does not support a reliable model split.
      routeYour label for how the work ran, such as “Current production route” or “Proposed pilot route.”
      requestsEvery provider call in the bucket, including additional attempts. Use application or gateway logs when the provider report omits it. Otherwise leave blank.
      input_tokensAll processed input tokens. When a provider splits uncached, cache read, and cache write tokens, add those parts here and keep the cache columns too. Leave blank if unavailable.
      cached_input_tokensInput tokens read from cache. Enter 0 only when the report confirms none; otherwise leave blank.
      cache_write_input_tokensInput tokens written to cache. Enter 0 only when the field is reported as zero or does not apply; otherwise leave blank.
      output_tokensAll output tokens. Leave blank if the source does not report them.
      provider_costThe cost for this row. Do not repeat one invoice total across several model rows.
      cost_basisprovider_reported for a billed amount, calculated for quantity × rate, or allocated when you assigned part of a shared bill.
      currencyA three-letter code such as USD. Both routes must use the same currency.
      Before you upload it
      • Both routes describe the same workload and use the same currency.
      • Each source amount appears once. Do not copy one invoice total onto every usage row.
      • Blank means the source did not supply the measure. Zero means the source reported zero or the measure does not apply.
      • The comparison upload reads this universal template. Use Upload what you have for supported Claude JSON, invoice PDFs, or guided structured-file mapping.
      02

      Add what happened to the work

      Use the same definition of “ready” for both routes and classify each result at the end of the review. A quick sample gives you a clearly labeled estimate; a complete work log supports a stronger review.

      One result is one unit of finished work, such as one reviewed summary, extracted invoice, resolved case, or completed task. It is not one API request. One result may require several model calls.

      Ready to useThe result cleared your rule, including after any correction you completed. Include all time spent.
      Needs correctionThe result has not cleared the rule and still needs material work.
      Needs escalationThe result could not be completed through the normal review path.
      Use the same quality rule on both routes. Enter the number of outputs in the period, then what you found in the reviewed sample.
      Current route
      Proposed route

      AI Cost Lens will extrapolate the sampled outcome rate and human time across the declared period. A user-selected sample stays directional and will not show a statistical range. Every result remains labeled as sampled, not observed production truth.

      Classify each row at the end of the review. If correction made the result ready, use ready_to_use and include the correction in human_minutes. model_requests counts every model call. retry_requests counts only the extra calls after the first attempt. A result produced with three calls has three model requests and two retries.

      Download work log
      Show me exactly what to put in the work log
      periodbaseline or proposed, matching the spend file.
      result_idA unique ID from your application or review record. If none exists, use a stable label such as base-001 or pilot-001.
      outcome_statusready_to_use, needs_correction, or needs_escalation, assigned at the end of review.
      model_requestsEvery provider call used for that result, including the first call and any additional attempts. Leave blank if your logs do not track it.
      retry_requestsOnly the additional model calls after the first attempt. Three model calls means two retries. Leave blank if your logs do not track it.
      human_minutesAll human review and correction time already spent on that result.

      01

      THE WORKLOAD

      Describe one call

      OpenAI raw text is counted locally with its o200k_base encoding. Other providers use a clearly labeled 4-characters-per-token estimate. Enter a known count below to override both.

      Enter planned calls before retries. Retry costs are included in the per-call and monthly estimates.

      Advanced cache assumptions

      Cached input is treated as a repeated prefix. Add refreshes only when the provider publishes a separate cache-write rate. A refresh replaces one cache-read call; it is not added on top of the same call.

      For explicit caches, token-hours equal cached tokens multiplied by retained hours across the month. Separate storage cost is added only where the provider publishes that rate. Zero means storage is excluded, not free.
